title: The Brain Still Listens to Stories During Surgery Sleep
summary:
When people have surgery, doctors may give them general anesthesia. This medicine makes them fully unconscious, so they do not feel or remember anything. Scientists thought the brain did little thinking then. A new study suggests it does more.

Researchers at Baylor College of Medicine in Texas studied patients having epilepsy surgery. They used tiny tools to record signals from hundreds of brain cells in the hippocampus. That part of the brain helps with learning and memory.

First, the scientists played repeating sounds with a different sound mixed in. The brain cells noticed the different sounds and got better at it over time.

Next, they played short stories. The brain activity showed patterns for different kinds of words, like nouns and verbs. It even held clues about which word would come next. "The brain appears to anticipate what comes next in a story, even without conscious awareness," said Dr. Sameer Sheth.
why_it_matters: It shows our brains are always busy, even when we are not awake.
